_note: Structural at-a-glance facts for Delhi's urban water supply, anchored on CAG Report No. 3 of 2025 (tabled 23 Mar 2026; audit period FY2017-18 to 2021-22), the Delhi Economic Survey 2023-24 Ch. 13, and DJB's own water page. Delhi is the platform's second 'pumped-from-far' city after Bengaluru - except nothing is pumped uphill: it arrives by gravity canal from five states, which is why the story stats emphasise distance and instruments, not lift. Source-wise availability figures are DJB's published raw-water splits (Economic Survey); production (~960 MGD = ~4,365 MLD) is the CAG-audited figure - the gap between claimed availability and audited production is itself a finding. Compiled 2026-07-20.

groundwater._provenance: DJB tube-wells + Ranney wells ~135 MGD (Economic Survey Ch. 13). No comprehensive tube-well register exists - its absence is a CAG finding; no defensible citywide estimate of private extraction is published, so no estimate_mld is stated.

wtps_summary._provenance: 9 WTPs (Wazirabad, Chandrawal, Haiderpur, Bhagirathi, Sonia Vihar, Nangloi, Okhla, Dwarka, Bawana) producing ~960 MGD against ~1,290+ MGD assessed requirement (CAG: potable shortage 25.79% in 2021-22)
wtps_summary._note: Capacity and average shown at the CAG-audited ~960 MGD production level; DJB's claimed source-wise availability (~998 MGD) is higher - the gap is a finding, see _note at file top.

distribution._provenance: NCT projected population ~2.1 crore (Economic Survey projections); DJB is the retail utility for all of it except the NDMC enclave (~3%) and Cantonment

demand._population_design_note: Draft MPD-2041 projection for 2041 (~2.92 crore; PRS Legislative Research summary of the Master Plan for Delhi 2041).
demand._demand_2034_note: Field name kept for the shared component; the figure is the MPD-2041 DESIGN-HORIZON target - 1,455 MGD for 2041 at the plan's reduced 50 GPCD norm (down from MPD-2021's 60 GPCD; Down to Earth on the draft MPD-2041). 1,455 MGD = ~6,614 MLD.
demand._demand_gap_note: Gap vs today's ~4,365 MLD (960 MGD) production - i.e. the 2041 target assuming no augmentation, which the CAG's own verdict on Renuka/Lakhwar/Kishau calls 'remote'.

_view_overrides.subtitle: Structural numbers from the CAG performance audit of the Delhi Jal Board (Report No. 3 of 2025), the Delhi Economic Survey 2023-24, and DJB's own water page. Refreshed when new audit or survey editions are published.
_view_overrides.demand_caption: MPD-2041 sets the 2041 target at 1,455 MGD - and that is with the norm CUT from 60 to 50 gallons per head. Against today's ~960 MGD production the plan-horizon gap is ~2,250 MLD, with the CAG calling augmentation prospects 'remote'.

allocation_context._provenance: 240 km = Bhakra (Gobind Sagar), Delhi's farthest source, delivered via the 102-km Munak carrier from Haryana. NRW 51-53% across FY18-22 (CAG); Economic Survey states 52.35% 'wasted or pilfered by tanker mafia'.

hero_copy.headline: No local storage: piped from five states, one 102-km canal, half the water unbilled
hero_copy.body: Delhi is a fundamentally dependent city. It owns no reservoir: ~90% of its raw water arrives from other states under a stack of instruments - the 1994 five-state Yamuna MoU at Wazirabad, the Munak carrier from Haryana (~70% of the lifeline), Bhakra storage from 240 km away, and Tehri's release riding the Upper Ganga Canal - with its own over-drafted groundwater making up the rest. Nine WTPs turn that into ~960 MGD against a ~1,290+ MGD requirement. What the instruments promise, what the canals deliver, and what the pipes lose on the way is the whole story of Delhi water.

hero_copy.nrw_sub: CAG FY18-22: Rs 4,988 crore of revenue lost; only 40% of production is billed
